about.title: Big Bear Lake Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grief in a mountain town of about 5,200 people is rarely private. Neighbors on Moonridge Road or Eureka Drive know when a family has lost someone, and the loss ripples through a community that is small in winter and crowded with visitors in summer. Public records for 2025 show 37 injury collisions in Big Bear Lake, 68 people hurt, and no traffic fatalities that year, with reported crashes clustering on Saturdays between 5 and 7 p.m. along Big Bear Boulevard and Route 18. Still, wrongful death claims here arise from more than roads: the lake, the slopes, short-term rentals, and steep driveways all bring their own hazards. Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring a claim, with certain dependents and heirs following. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it is shorter when a public agency is involved. Our team handles these claims directly and offers a free initial review.

whyChoose.title: Why Big Bear Lake Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before any decision is made.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Contacting us early keeps those options open.

items.title: A civil path, separate from any criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not prosecutors act, your family may pursue funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance through a civil claim. We take these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative died in a boating accident on Big Bear Lake. Can that be a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: It may be, if another person's or company's negligence contributed to the death. Rental operators, other boaters, and property owners can each carry responsibility depending on the facts. We can review the incident report and marina records to see what happened. Because Big Bear Lake involves both local and public agencies, the filing deadline could be much shorter than two years.

items.question: Do I have to wait for the criminal case to end before filing?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, regardless of whether charges are filed or how they turn out. Waiting can actually put the two-year deadline at risk. Speaking with us early lets your family understand both paths at once.

items.question: What do we charge to review your case?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free initial consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You are under no obligation after the first conversation.
